processing: Orthodox Darjeeling black tea, with about a quarter of the area under clonal bushes including AV2 and P312; first flush is lightly oxidised, as usual in Darjeeling.
harvest_season: The season opens in February, unusually early, and the early first flush is the garden's most prized picking.
appearance_dry: As with other clonal Darjeeling first flushes, light green and silvery tipped leaf.
appearance_liquor: A pale golden amber, typical of Darjeeling first flush.
appearance_wet: Typically bright green leaf with coppery edges.
taste_profile: Few independent notes exist; as with other early Darjeeling first flushes, expect a fresh, floral and lightly brisk cup.

brewing.notes: General first flush guidance: use cooler water for very green lots, no milk, and short steeps.

vintage_note: Sold by year, flush and often a lot name. Its early first flush picking is what earns a premium, so check the invoice date or season. Drink it within a year or so of picking.
description:
North Tukvar, also called Singla, is a low-lying Darjeeling garden known for coming in first. Its reported altitude runs only from 1,500 to 2,800 feet, and its slopes cover about 195 hectares.

About a quarter of the area is planted with clonal bushes such as AV2 and P312. The season starts as early as February, which gives the garden some of the first teas of the year and a premium price.

As is usual for early first flush, expect something green, floral and fresh instead of a robust black tea. Be careful with hot water and long steeps, which make these teas sharp, and skip the milk.

This garden shares its owner and part of its name with Puttabong, once called Tukvar, so read the label carefully. The year and season matter more here than almost anywhere, since early lots are what the garden is known for.
history:
North Tukvar is described as one of the earliest commercial gardens in Darjeeling, started on an experimental basis in the early 1850s and producing commercially from 1856.

Jay Shree Tea, of the Birla family, acquired the estate in 1995.
